title: 11. Projects: Generators Iterators
summary: Create a memory-efficient log file analyzer using generators to process large log files without loading them entirely into memory.

Keep a short README with assumptions and tradeoffs

sections.title: Project 1: Log File Analyzer
sections.body:
**Difficulty**: Medium

### Description

Create a memory-efficient log file analyzer using generators to process large log files without loading them entirely into memory.

### Requirements

1. Read log files line by line using generators
2. Filter logs by severity level (INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
3. Extract timestamp, level, and message
4. Generate statistics (count by level)
5. Find patterns in error messages

### Features to Implement

- Generator to read file line by line
- Generator to parse log entries
- Generator to filter by severity
- Generator to extract specific time ranges
- Pipeline to process logs efficiently

### Sample Log Format

```
2024-01-15 10:30:45 INFO User logged in
2024-01-15 10:31:12 ERROR Database connection failed
2024-01-15 10:31:45 WARNING High memory usage detected
```

### Bonus Challenges

- Handle multiple log files
- Generate daily/hourly statistics
- Create alerts for critical patterns
- Export filtered results

sections.title: Project 3: Custom CSV Parser


- Support different encodings
- Create CSV writer
- Add data validation

sections.body:

sections.title: Project 9: Pipeline Framework
sections.body:
**Difficulty**: Hard

### Description

Create a reusable framework for building data processing pipelines using generators.

### Requirements

1. Composable pipeline stages
2. Error handling
3. Logging and monitoring
4. Performance metrics
5. Parallel processing support

### Pipeline Operations

- Map: Transform each item
- Filter: Select items
- Reduce: Aggregate results
- Batch: Group items
- Flatten: Unnest structures

### Example Usage

```python
pipeline = Pipeline()
    .map(transform)
    .filter(condition)
    .batch(10)
    .process(data)
```

### Bonus Challenges

- Add caching layer
- Implement backpressure
- Create visualization
- Add retry logic

sections.title: Tips for All Projects
sections.body:
### Best Practices

1. ✅ Always use generators for large data
2. ✅ Document what each generator yields
3. ✅ Handle `StopIteration` properly
4. ✅ Test with small and large datasets
5. ✅ Profile memory usage
6. ✅ Consider infinite vs finite generators
7. ✅ Use `yield from` for delegation
8. ✅ Implement proper cleanup

### Testing Strategy

- Unit test each generator independently
- Test pipeline integration
- Verify memory efficiency
- Check edge cases (empty data, single item, etc.)
- Performance benchmarks

### Performance Optimization

- Use generator expressions for simple operations
- Avoid materializing entire sequence
- Consider caching when appropriate
- Profile to find bottlenecks
- Use itertools for efficiency

**Happy Coding! Master generators through these practical projects! 🚀**
